mainTopic: Medical remedies (hemorrhoids, ear pain) and which dangerous conditions, especially eye problems, may be treated on שבת
overview: This עמוד opens with practical medical advice. First comes a remedy for hemorrhoids, with backup cures for the deeper kind. Next is the cure taught to רבי אבהו for ear pain: lukewarm fluid from a goat's kidney, followed by a chain of fallback cures and a memory aid about moist and dry treatments. The גמרא then returns to healing on שבת. רבי חנינא allows putting the ears back in place, and there are two versions of which method is allowed. רב rules that a dangerously sick eye may be treated on שבת, and רבי יעקב reports from רב יהודה that this applies even if it needs grinding and carrying. A story about רב שמואל בר יהודה and שמואל's maidservant shows the source of the ruling. The reason given is that the eye is linked to the heart. רב יהודה then lists which eye problems count, and the עמוד ends with his warnings about bathhouses and hot and cold remedies, which finish on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A remedy for hemorrhoids
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי, or some say רבי אסי, gives a two-part remedy for פיקעא: burned ice-plant seeds spread on the sores, and a bramble kernel placed against the anus.
steps.simpleTranslation: For hemorrhoids, רבי אמי (some say רבי אסי) told him: bring seven red ice-plant seeds and tie them into a shirt collar. Wrap a strip of hair around the bundle, dip it in white naphtha, burn it, and spread the ashes on the sores. In the meantime, bring the kernel of a bramble fruit and place its crevice against his crevice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא records the practical advice a חכם gave to someone suffering from hemorrhoids. The beginning of this story is at the end of the previous עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts to the cure. The first is ashes made from burned seeds, spread on the sores. The second is a bramble kernel placed directly on the sore spot while the first treatment is going on. The גמרא is unsure who gave the advice, so it gives two names.

keyTerms.meaning: Crevice; here, hemorrhoids or the sore area of the anus
He instructed him (gave him a ruling or advice)

phrases.english: from hemorrhoids.
Rabbi Ami instructed him,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי אוֹרִי לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Asi instructed him:
he should bring seven seeds of worm-red ice plant,
and tie them in the collar of a shirt,
and wrap a strip of hair around it,
and dip it in white naphtha,
and burn it and spread the ashes upon the sores.
In the meantime,
he should bring the kernel of a bramble fruit,
and place its crevice against his crevice.
phrases.notes: The first "crevice" is the split in the kernel; the second is the person's sore spot.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hemorrhoids are treated with ashes of burned ice-plant seeds, along with a bramble kernel placed against the sore.

steps.title: What about the deeper, lower hemorrhoid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the remedy to the outer (upper) crevice and asks what to do for the inner (lower) one.
steps.simpleTranslation: This only works for the upper crevice. What should be done for the lower crevice?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the remedy it just gave has a limit. It then asks a question, which sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kernel can only be placed against an outer sore. So the גמרא needs a different treatment for a sore deeper inside the body.

phrases.english: And this applies only to the upper crevice;
what about the lower crevice?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the remedy of step 1 to the outer case and asks about the inner case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to treat a hemorrhoid deep inside the rectum.

steps.title: Melted goat fat for the lower crevice
steps.stepSummary: For the inner sore, melt the fat of a goat that has never given birth and apply it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should bring the fat of a goat that has not yet given birth, melt it, and apply it there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 2 with a remedy for the inner sore.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Melted fat is a liquid, so it can reach a spot that a kernel cannot. That is why it suits the inner sore.

phrases.english: He should bring the fat of a goat that has not opened,
phrases.notes: "Not opened" means the goat has never given birth.

phrases.english: and melt it and apply it there.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Apply melted fat of a goat that has never given birth.

steps.title: Backup remedies if goat fat is not available
steps.stepSummary: Three fallback options: burned shade-dried pumpkin leaves, snail shells, or oil mixed with wax smeared on worn flax (summer) or cotton (winter).
steps.simpleTranslation: If not, bring three pumpkin leaves dried in the shade, burn them, and spread the ashes on the sore. If not, bring snail shells. If not, bring oil mixed with wax and smear it on worn flax cloth in summer, or worn cotton in winter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists other choices to use, one after another, if the earlier remedy is not possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each "ואי לא" opens the next option down. The last option even changes depending on the season: flax cloth in summer and cotton in winter.

keyTerms.meaning: And if not (if this isn't available)

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא, לַיְיתֵי תְּלָת טַרְפֵא קָרָא
phrases.english: And if not, he should bring three pumpkin leaves
that were dried in the shade,
and burn them and spread the ashes on the sore.
And if not, he should bring snail shells.
And if not, he brings oil with wax,
and smears it on worn flax cloth in summer,
and on worn cotton in winter.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ranked list of substitute remedies.
steps.whatToRemember: For hemorrhoids: kernel and ashes for the outer sore; goat fat for the inner sore; then pumpkin-leaf ashes, snail shells, or oil and wax on cloth as backups.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's ear pain
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו had ear pain, and רבי יוחנן (some say the בית מדרש) told him how to treat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו had pain in his ear. רבי יוחנן instructed him, and some say the study hall instructed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new medical story about ear pain. It does not yet say what the advice was, so this step sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like step 1, the גמרא gives two versions of who gave the advice: רבי יוחנן, or the חכמים of the בית מדרש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu had pain in his ear;
Rabbi Yochanan instructed him,
and some say the study hall instructed him.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבהו received a remedy for ear pain.

steps.title: What was the advice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what remedy רבי אבהו was given.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he instruct him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the content of the advice. This sets up the answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 only said that advice was given. Here the גמרא asks what that advice actually was.

phrases.english: What did he instruct him?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual remedy given for ear pain.

steps.title: אביי's mother: the kidney is for the ear
steps.stepSummary: The advice follows what אביי reported from his mother: the kidney was created for the ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was like what אביי said: My mother told me that the kidney was created only for the ear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer by quoting a known principle: kidneys are especially good for healing the ear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "only for the ear" is an exaggeration. It means kidneys are extremely helpful for the ear. This is the reason behind the recipe that comes later.

phrases.english: Like that which Abaye said:
My mother told me:
The kidney was created only for the ear.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The remedy is based on the kidney, which is especially good for the ear.

steps.title: The doctor מניומי agrees
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that the physician מניומי said every liquid harms the ear except kidney fluid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: מניומי the doctor told me that all liquids are harmful to the ear except the fluid of the kidneys.
steps.whatsHappening: A second source backs up the idea that kidney fluid is good for the ear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's mother said kidneys help the ear. מניומי adds a warning: every other liquid is harmful to the ear. That makes kidney fluid the one safe and useful choice.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא: אֲמַר לִי מִנְיוֹמֵי אָסְיָא —
phrases.english: And Rava said: Minyumi the doctor told me:
All liquids are harmful to the ear,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean "liquids."

phrases.english: except for the fluid of the kidneys.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: אֲמַר לִי מִנְיוֹמֵי אָסְיָא
steps.raayaObject: That kidney fluid is the right remedy for the ear.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The physician מניומי, as reported by רבא.

steps.title: The kidney recipe for ear pain
steps.stepSummary: Take a bald goat's kidney, cut it crosswise, set it on dying coals, and put the lukewarm fluid that comes out into the ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should bring the kidney of a bald goat, tear it lengthwise and widthwise, and place it on dimming coals. The fluid that comes out should be put in his ear, not cold and not hot, but lukewarm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the exact steps of the remedy that was taught to רבי אבהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kidney is cut both ways so its fluid can come out. Weak, dying coals heat it gently. The fluid must be lukewarm, because hot or cold liquid could hurt the ear.
steps.whatToRemember: For ear pain, the גמרא uses lukewarm fluid from a gently heated goat's kidney. This rests on אביי's mother and the doctor מניומי.

phrases.english: He should bring the kidney of a bald goat,
and tear it lengthwise and widthwise,
and place it on dimming coals,
and the fluid that comes out of it
he should put into his ear,

phrases.aramaic: לָא קָרִירֵי וְלָא חַמִּימֵי, אֶלָּא פָּשׁוֹרֵי.
phrases.english: not cold and not hot, but lukewarm.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The remedy for רבי אבהו's ear was lukewarm fluid from a bald goat's kidney, heated on dying coals.

steps.title: First backup cure: melted beetle fat
steps.stepSummary: If the kidney cure is not available, melt the fat of a large beetle and put it in the ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, he should bring the fat of a large beetle, melt it, and put it in the ear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a backup cure in case the goat-kidney cure from the last step cannot be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ואי לא' mean 'if you can't do the previous one.' This opens a chain of fallback cures. Each one is a replacement, not an extra step added to the kidney cure.

keyTerms.meaning: And if not (if the previous cure isn't possible)

steps.confusionAlert: Each 'ואי לא' introduces a different cure to use instead. Do not read these as one long cure with many steps.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא, לַיְיתֵי תַּרְבָּא דְּחִיפּוּשְׁתָּא גַּמְלָנִיתָא,
phrases.english: And if not, he should bring the fat of a large beetle,
and melt it and put it into it (the ear).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא, לַיְיתֵי תַּרְבָּא דְּחִיפּוּשְׁתָּא גַּמְלָנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a substitute for the kidney cure of step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Melted large-beetle fat put in the ear is a backup cure.

steps.title: Second backup cure: oil and seven burning alfalfa wicks
steps.stepSummary: Fill the ear with oil, light seven alfalfa wicks tied with garlic ends, and hold the ear near the flame one wick at a time, staying away from drafts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, he should fill his ear with oil, make seven wicks of alfalfa, bring dried garlic ends, tie them on with a strip of hair at one end, and set them on fire. He places the other end in his ear and puts his ear opposite the flame. He must be careful of drafts. He takes one wick away and puts the next one in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another fallback cure, this time using oil and warm burning wicks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This cure works with warmth: the oil sits in the ear while the wick's heat reaches it. The seven wicks are used one after another, replacing each as it burns. The warning about drafts is added because wind would undo the warming.

phrases.english: And if not, he should fill his ear with oil,
and make seven wicks of alfalfa,
and bring dried garlic ends,
and tie them with a strip of hair at one end,
phrases.notes: He ties the garlic onto the wicks.

phrases.english: and set them on fire,
and the other end is placed in the ear,
and he should place his ear opposite the flame,
and he should be careful of drafts,
and take one away and put one in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next fallback cure in the chain
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil in the ear plus seven burning alfalfa wicks, used one at a time, while avoiding drafts.

steps.title: A second version of the wick cure: wax wicks with alfalfa oil
steps.stepSummary: Another version says to use seven wax wicks smeared with alfalfa oil, one end in the fire and one in the ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: And if not, he should bring seven wax wicks and smear them with alfalfa oil. He puts one end in the fire and one end in his ear, takes one away and puts one in, and is careful of drafts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the cure it just described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לישנא אחרינא' means the same cure was passed down in another form. Here the wicks are made of wax and the alfalfa becomes an oil smeared on them, instead of alfalfa wicks with oil inside the ear.

phrases.english: Another version:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא, לַיְיתֵי שַׁב פְּתִילָתָא בִּיקְרָא,
phrases.english: And if not, he should bring seven wicks of wax,
and smear them with alfalfa oil,
and put one end in the fire
and one end in his ear,
and take one away and put one in,
and he should be careful of drafts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the step 11 cure
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven wax wicks smeared with alfalfa oil, used one at a time, avoiding drafts.

steps.title: Third backup cure: uncombed fiber held near the fire
steps.stepSummary: Put dried, uncombed fiber in the ear and hold the ear toward the fire, avoiding drafts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, he should bring fiber that was dried but not combed and put it in his ear, then hold his ear toward the fire, and be careful of drafts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives yet another fallback cure, again using warmth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simpler warming cure: the fiber sits in the ear and the fire warms it. The draft warning repeats because, as with the wicks, wind would cancel out the warmth.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא, לַיְיתֵי אוּדְרָא דְּנָדָא דְּלָא מְשַׁקֵּף
phrases.english: And if not, he should bring fiber that was dried and not combed
and put it in (his ear),
and hold his ear toward the fire,
and he should be careful of drafts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא, לַיְיתֵי אוּדְרָא דְּנָדָא דְּלָא מְשַׁקֵּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next fallback cure in the chain
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Uncombed dried fiber in the ear, ear toward the fire, avoiding drafts.

steps.title: Fourth backup cure: an old reed with rock salt
steps.stepSummary: Take a hundred-year-old reed tube, salt it with rock salt, burn it, and stick it in the ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, he should bring the tube of an old reed, one hundred years old, salt it with rock salt, burn it, and stick it in his ear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last fallback cure, this one dry instead of oily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier cures that use oil or fat, this one uses a very dry reed, salted and burned. This sets up the memory aid in the next step about moist and dry cures.

keyTerms.meaning: The hollow tube of a reed

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא, לַיְיתֵי גּוּבְתָּא דְּקַנְיָא עַתִּיקָא
phrases.english: And if not, he should bring the tube of an old reed
one hundred years old,
phrases.notes: Meaning it was cut from the ground that long ago, so it is completely dry.

phrases.english: and salt it with rock salt,
and burn it and stick it on (in the ear).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא, לַיְיתֵי גּוּבְתָּא דְּקַנְיָא עַתִּיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final fallback cure in the chain
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A salted, burned hundred-year-old reed tube is stuck in the ear.

steps.title: Memory aid: moist cures for dry problems, dry cures for moist problems
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a way to remember which cures fit which ear problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: And your memory aid: moist for dry, and dry for moist.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the list of ear cures with a short memory aid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oily and fatty cures are for a dry ear problem, and the dry cure, like the reed, is for a wet or oozing ear problem. This organizes the whole list into two groups.
steps.whatToRemember: The ear cures fall into two groups: wet cures, like oil and fat, for a dry ear, and dry cures, like the burned reed, for a wet ear.

phrases.english: And your memory aid: moist for dry,
and dry for moist.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the whole list of cures
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Match the cure to the problem: moist cures for dry ailments, dry cures for moist ailments.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: one may raise the ears on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר זוטרא quotes רבי חנינא that it is allowed to raise the ears into place on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר זוטרא said in the name of רבי חנינא: One may raise the ears on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of medical treatment on שבת and brings a new ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Raising the ears' means putting back into place something near the ears that slipped down, like a slipped jaw. רבי חנינא allows this on שבת, even though healing on שבת is usually limited.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר זוּטְרָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Zutra said that Rabbi Chanina said:
One may raise the ears on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: This means putting back what slipped out of place near the ears, like setting a slipped jaw.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר זוּטְרָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ear cures and returns to treatment on שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Raising the ears into place is allowed on שבת.

steps.title: רב שמואל בר יהודה: by hand, not with medicine
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה limits the ruling: only by hand, not with medicine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יהודה taught: By hand, but not with medicine.
steps.whatsHappening: A teaching is brought that narrows רבי חנינא's ruling and says how it may be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission to raise the ears is real, but only one method is allowed. By this version, using hands is fine, while using medicine is not allowed.

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda taught:
By hand, but not with medicine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the method allowed by step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Raising the ears on שבת is allowed only by hand, not with medicine.

steps.title: Others say the opposite: with medicine, not by hand
steps.stepSummary: A second version flips the teaching: medicine is allowed, but not the hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: With medicine, but not by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב שמואל בר יהודה's teaching that says the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that raising the ears on שבת is allowed in some way. They argue only about which method is the allowed one.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion against רבי חנינא. It is another version of the limit on how to do it, the reverse of step 17.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
With medicine, but not by hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse version of step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Raising the ears on שבת is allowed with medicine, not by hand.

steps.title: Why not by hand?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the second version.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why, by the second version, one may not raise the ears by hand. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the hand seems simpler and milder than medicine, so forbidding it needs a reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the last version: why not by hand?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why raising the ears by hand is forbidden by the second version

steps.title: Because the hand might injure the ear
steps.stepSummary: Doing it by hand might injure the ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he might injure it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that using the hand could cause an injury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hurting the body by hand could be a more serious שבת problem, from the תורה, while using medicine is only a rabbinic concern. So this version allows the milder method, medicine, and forbids the riskier one, the hand.
steps.whatToRemember: Raising the ears on שבת is allowed. The two versions argue only about the method; by the second, the hand is forbidden because it might cause an injury.

phrases.english: He might injure it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Using the hand risks injuring the ear, which would be a more serious violation.

steps.title: A dangerously sick eye may be treated on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that an eye in serious trouble may have כחל put on it on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: An eye that 'rebelled' may be painted with eye medicine on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב: a badly sick eye may be treated with כחל on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we do not treat ordinary sickness on שבת. Here רב allows it, which tells us he treats this eye problem as more than a small matter. The next steps will ask how far this permission goes.

keyTerms.meaning: An eye that 'rebelled', meaning an eye with a serious, dangerous problem
To paint it with כחל, a kind of eye paint used as medicine

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Zutra bar Toviyya said that Rav said:
An eye that rebelled,
phrases.notes: This means an eye in serious trouble, so bad that it could pop out.

phrases.english: it is permitted to paint it with eye paint on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ears in Steps 16-20 to a new body part, the eye.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dangerously sick eye may be treated with כחל on שבת.

steps.title: The first understanding: only if no real מלאכה is needed
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים first assume רב only allowed it when the medicine was ready from before שבת and did not need to be carried through the public area.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from this: That applies only when the ingredients were ground the day before. But grinding them on שבת, or bringing them through רשות הרבים, is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים suggest a limited reading of רב's ruling. This sets up the next step, which will reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grinding (טוחן) and carrying in רשות הרבים are מלאכות forbidden by the תורה. The first thought is that רב only allowed putting on medicine that was already made, not doing real מלאכה for it.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it (a first assumption that is often rejected)
From yesterday, meaning from before שבת
The public domain, where carrying on שבת is forbidden by the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final הלכה. It is only the first thought, and the very next step pushes it away.

phrases.english: They understood from it:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הוּא דִּשְׁחִקִי סַמָּנִין מֵאֶתְמוֹל,
phrases.english: These words apply only where the ingredients were ground yesterday,
but to grind them on Shabbat
or to bring them through the public domain — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a narrow reading of רב's ruling from Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First assumption: only medicine already prepared may be used, with no מלאכה forbidden by the תורה.

steps.title: רבי יעקב: even grinding and carrying are allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב reports from רב יהודה that even grinding on שבת and carrying through רשות הרבים is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the חכמים, named רבי יעקב, said to him: It was explained to me by רב יהודה that even grinding on שבת and bringing it through רשות הרבים is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב rejects the narrow reading from Step 22. He says the permission is full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even מלאכות forbidden by the תורה are allowed, this eye problem must count as a danger to life (פיקוח נפש). That is the only thing that pushes aside the תורה's שבת laws. The גמרא will explain why an eye is so serious in Step 30.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the eye case is treated as פיקוח נפש, not just a small discomfort.

phrases.english: One of the Rabbis said to him,
and Rabbi Ya'akov was his name:
To me it was explained by Rav Yehuda:
Even to grind on Shabbat
and to bring it through the public domain — is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב שְׁמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the limited reading of Step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole limitation suggested in Step 22.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב יהודה clearly taught that even מלאכות forbidden by the תורה are allowed for this eye.

steps.title: רב יהודה permits, and רב שמואל בר יהודה mocks
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב יהודה allowed eye paint on שבת, and רב שמואל בר יהודה said that following him means breaking שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה allowed painting an eye on שבת. רב שמואל בר יהודה said to the people: Whoever listens to יהודה is breaking שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story showing רב יהודה's ruling in action, and someone who strongly disagreed with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שמואל בר יהודה thought the ruling was too lenient and amounted to חילול שבת. The story will show what happened when he needed the ruling himself.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה שְׁרָא לְמִיכְחַל עֵינָא בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda permitted painting an eye on Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda said to them:
Whoever listens to Yehuda desecrates Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה שְׁרָא לְמִיכְחַל עֵינָא בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רב יהודה's ruling from Step 23 being used and attacked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה allowed eye paint on שבת; רב שמואל בר יהודה called it חילול שבת.

steps.title: His own eye hurts, so he asks
steps.stepSummary: Later רב שמואל בר יהודה's eye hurt, and he sent to רב יהודה to ask if he may treat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end his own eye hurt. He sent to רב יהודה: Is it permitted or forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The story turns: the one who mocked the ruling now needs it, and asks רב יהודה. This sets up רב יהודה's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is simple: may I treat my eye on שבת? The irony is that he is asking the very person he criticized.

keyTerms.meaning: He felt pain in his eye

phrases.english: In the end, he felt pain in his eye.
He sent to him: Is it permitted or forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from Step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב שמואל בר יהודה may treat his own eye on שבת.

steps.title: Allowed for everyone, but not for you
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers: for everyone it is allowed, but for you it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to him: For everyone else it is permitted; for you it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers sharply. He says the הלכה allows it, but since you mocked it, you may not use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה itself does not change: it is permitted. רב יהודה is answering the man's mockery, not changing the rule.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the הלכה is different for different people. רב יהודה is reacting to how he was treated.

phrases.english: He sent back to him:
For everyone, it is permitted;
for you, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Since you called my ruling breaking שבת, you can't now rely on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is permitted in general, but רב יהודה refuses to let the mocker use it.

steps.title: It is not my own ruling, it comes from מר שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה adds that the ruling is not his own; it comes from his teacher מר שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is this my own idea? It is the ruling of מר שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה defends his ruling by showing it comes from a great authority, מר שמואל. This sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שמואל בר יהודה treated the ruling as רב יהודה's personal leniency. רב יהודה answers that he is only passing on what שמואל taught.

phrases.english: And is it from me?
phrases.notes: These are still רב יהודה's words in his message.

phrases.english: It is the ruling of Mar Shmuel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the ruling mocked in Step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's permission to treat the eye on שבת.

steps.title: The maidservant's eye and שמואל's teaching
steps.stepSummary: A maidservant in שמואל's house had an inflamed eye on שבת, nobody treated it, and her eye burst. The next day שמואל taught that a sick eye may be treated on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A maidservant in מר שמואל's house had an inflamed eye on שבת. She cried out, but no one paid attention, and her eye burst. The next day מר שמואל went out and taught: An eye that rebelled may be painted on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story behind שמואל's ruling. A real tragedy showed him how dangerous an eye problem can be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody treated her because they thought it was forbidden on שבת. The harm that came showed שמואל this is a real danger, so he taught publicly that it must be treated.

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא אַמְתָּא דַּהֲוַאי בֵּי מָר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: There was a certain maidservant in the house of Mar Shmuel
whose eye became inflamed on Shabbat.
She screamed, and there was no one who paid attention to her.
Her eye burst.
The next day, Mar Shmuel went out and taught:
An eye that rebelled — it is permitted to paint it on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אַמְתָּא דַּהֲוַאי בֵּי מָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the story proving the ruling is שמואל's, as claimed in Step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל taught that an eye that rebelled may be treated on שבת.

steps.title: Why is an eye so serious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind allowing eye treatment on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why an eye problem is serious enough to override שבת. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only danger to life pushes aside שבת. An eye seems like just one body part, so the גמרא wants to know why it counts as life-threatening.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind שמואל's teaching in Step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a sick eye counts as פיקוח נפש.

steps.title: The eye is connected to the heart
steps.stepSummary: The cords of the eye are connected to the heart, so danger to the eye is danger to life.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the cords of the eye are attached to the openings of the heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the eye is linked to the heart, so a serious eye problem can threaten a person's life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of this link, a dangerous eye problem is not just about losing an eye. It is פיקוח נפש, which explains why even מלאכות forbidden by the תורה are allowed (Step 23).
steps.whyThisMatters: This reason is why the הלכה treats serious eye problems as פיקוח נפש on שבת.

phrases.english: Because the cords of the eye
are attached to the openings of the heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The eye is connected to the heart, so a serious eye problem endangers life.

steps.title: Which eye problems count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for examples of an eye problem that counts as 'rebelled'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Such as what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which kinds of eye trouble are serious enough. This sets up רב יהודה's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every sore eye is dangerous. The גמרא needs a clear definition of עין שמרדה.

phrases.english: Such as what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define the case after the reason was given in Step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which eye conditions count as עין שמרדה.

steps.title: רב יהודה's list of dangerous eye problems
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה lists discharge, pricking, blood, tearing, inflammation and the start of infection as dangerous, but not the end of an infection or treatment just to sharpen eyesight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Such as discharge, pricking, blood, tears, inflammation, and the beginning of an infection. This leaves out the end of an infection and brightening the eyes, which are not included.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a list of eye problems that may be treated on שבת, and two that may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Problems that are active and getting worse count as dangerous. An infection that is already healing, or treatment only to see better, is not dangerous, so it may not be done on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: A serious eye problem is פיקוח נפש because the eye is linked to the heart, so even מלאכות forbidden by the תורה are allowed. But only active, dangerous problems count, not a healing infection or treatment just for sharper sight.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Such as discharge, pricking, blood,
tearing, and inflammation, and the beginning of an infection,
to exclude the end of an infection
and brightening the eye — which are not included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Active problems (discharge, pricking, blood, tearing, inflammation, start of infection) count; the end of an infection and treatment only for sharper sight do not.

steps.title: Five conditions where the bathhouse is dangerous
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה lists five conditions where entering a bathhouse puts a person's life at risk: a hornet sting, a thorn prick, an abscess, a painful eye, and a fever.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: someone stung by a hornet, someone pricked by a thorn, someone with an abscess, someone whose eye hurts, and someone with a fever should not go to the bathhouse. For all of them it is dangerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב יהודה: a list of five sick people for whom a hot bathhouse is a danger to life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps were about eye problems that count as a danger to life. Now רב יהודה widens the picture with general medical warnings. The point is that a bathhouse can make these conditions much worse, so for these people it counts as סכנה, real danger, and not just discomfort.

keyTerms.meaning: A hornet, here meaning a hornet sting
An abscess, a swelling full of pus

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says:
A hornet sting, and one whom a thorn pricked,
and an abscess, and one whose eye hurts him,
and one who is overcome by a fever,
for all of them, the bathhouse is a danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יהודה's medical teachings from the eye discussion, now moving to dangers of the bathhouse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a hornet sting, a thorn prick, an abscess, eye pain, or fever, entering a bathhouse is a danger to life.

steps.title: Radish for fever, beets for chills
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה teaches that radish helps a fever and beets help chills, but switching them around is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: Radish is good for a fever, and beets are good for chills. But eating them the other way around is dangerous.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה continues with food advice: which vegetable to eat for fever and which for chills.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gives a matching pair: one food for a hot illness and one for a cold illness. Then he adds a warning that mixing them up, radish for chills or beets for fever, is not just useless but dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: Can mean radish, and can also mean fever (wordplay)
The reverse, the opposite way around

steps.confusionAlert: The same word חַמָּה appears twice with two meanings. The first one means radish, and the second one means fever.

phrases.english: Radish for a fever,
and beets for chills,
but the reverse is a danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same statement of רב יהודה, moving from bathhouse dangers to food remedies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Radish helps fever and beets help chills; using them the opposite way is dangerous.

steps.title: Hot and cold remedies for stings and thorns
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה teaches that hot things help a scorpion sting and cold things help a hornet sting, with the reverse being dangerous. He then begins a new pair: hot water for a thorn, and cold for something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hot things are good for a scorpion sting and cold things are good for a hornet sting, but the other way around is dangerous. Hot water is good for a thorn, and cold water is good for...
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives more hot-and-cold pairs of treatments, and the text stops in the middle of the last pair, which finishes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Same pattern as before: two similar problems need opposite treatments. A scorpion sting and a hornet sting seem alike, yet one needs hot and the other cold, and mixing them up is dangerous. The thorn pair is only half finished here.

keyTerms.meaning: Hot things (hot food or hot water)
A scorpion, here meaning a scorpion sting

phrases.english: Hot things for a scorpion sting
and cold things for a hornet sting,
but the reverse is a danger.
Hot water for a thorn, and cold water...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same pattern of paired remedies with a warning against reversing them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hot things help a scorpion sting and cold things help a hornet sting; the reverse is dangerous. Hot water helps a thorn.
